attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, endorsed.

semantics.note: Fair core: the two papers demonstrated reasoning/generalization failures. The coffin metaphor and 'unfairly dismissed' are rhetoric, not scored.

contract.note: Plain reading (demonstrated failures in tested models, not universal inability) is ordinary and fair to the speaker's words.

evidence.note: Apple v3 (20 Nov 2025, pre-post) reports complete accuracy collapse beyond certain complexities in tested reasoning models.
Pre-post version of the CoT mirage paper shows CoT effectiveness falls sharply under distribution shift in controlled experiments.
Replication undercuts River Crossing results (unsolvable instances) but confirms Tower of Hanoi failures; qualifies, does not invalidate all findings.

reviews.rationale: Both papers, in versions available before the post, empirically report reasoning/generalization failures. The methodological critique (e3) invalidates part of Apple's results but leaves other failures intact, so the support condition is met.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence. The $2T/2030 figure is cited from Zitron, but Marcus endorses the conditional.

semantics.note: Antecedent kept. The 2030 horizon comes from the quoted Zitron headline the sentence refers to, which is a reasonable carry-over.

contract.note: Reading as 2030 annual realized revenue and 'new ideas' as beyond pure scaling is reasonable. The antecedent and necessity are hard to operationalize.

evidence.note: Bain's 2025 estimate of revenue needed by 2030. It is not achieved revenue, has a different population, and says nothing about the antecedent.

reviews.rationale: The deadline (end of 2030) is after the evaluation date. The antecedent (that Marcus/Sutskever are right about LLM limits) is not established, and no early-resolution event exists. Not scored.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words, though he also cites Sutskever's view of the Kaplan laws.

semantics.note: The scored core, 'returns appear to be diminishing', is hedged ('appear'). Only the minor 'measurable improvements' clause is firm.

contract.note: The contract applies a plain reading and support/contradiction tests to hedged language. Policy bars this, so the hedged trend should not be scored.

evidence.note: Kaplan 2020 is about loss scaling. It does not address late-2025 downstream returns.
Epoch (Sept 2025): gains per order of magnitude are consistent with expected scaling. Does not settle diminishing returns per unit of compute.
Pre-post v2: short-task metrics may hide long-horizon gains. Challenges the inference but is not a representative compute comparison.

reviews.rationale: The scored proposition rests on 'returns appear to be diminishing', a hedged statement, so policy says it is not scored. The packet's evidence would not settle it anyway, since the result depends on the metric and how a compute increment is defined.

attribution.note: Marcus's own firm statement. The Sutskever reference is supporting attribution.

semantics.note: Firm clause 'none of these experiments has solved core issues' is correctly isolated. The hedged returns clause is excluded.

contract.note: 'Solved' read as no longer a basic limitation of frontier models; benchmark wins do not count. This is an ordinary, fair reading.

evidence.note: OpenAI-affiliated paper (Sept 2025) says hallucinations persist in state-of-the-art systems.
Apple (June 2025): frontier reasoning models collapse on complex planning puzzles.
Sutskever (25 Nov 2025) calls models' poor generalization a fundamental, obvious weakness.
ARC Prize post-dates the post (Dec 2025). It agrees reasoning flaws remain but is context only.
IMO gold-level results show major reasoning progress on one task, not a general solution.

reviews.rationale: Pre-post evidence from lab researchers, Apple, and Sutskever shows hallucination, generalization and reasoning/planning remained substantial limits in late 2025. IMO progress does not show any of these was solved.
